Buildings at Donald Trump's state fair have been exposed as being fake

The buildings at President Donald Trump's Great American State Fair have been exposed as fakes as the disastrous multi-day event continues.

Photos and videos have emerged on social media, offering close-ups of the buildings that adorn the 16-day event at the National Mall in Washington, D.C. One clip revealed that the "buildings" are actually just structures with printed sheets stapled on.

Another clip showed a similar close-up of Trump's golden arch, a mock-up of the United States Triumphal Arch celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence. "The Golden Arch is their pride and joy, but look at it up close!!!" wrote one person on X. It comes as Trump was accused of a "very unhealthy" relationship with his blonde 34-year-old aide.

The video reveals that the arch also features printed sheets stapled to a structure. Someone else posted a video revealing that the columned buildings at the event weren't three-dimensional.

Some of the columns didn't even reach the floor and had to be held up with sticks. "That’s how the Romans did it," joked one person.

Columns don't reach the ground and have to be held up with sticks

"They would carve stone columns by hand and then balance them on scrap wood that Tommy had in his truck." Another person said this was the end result "when you p--s off every creative person in the United States."

Someone else joked, "They are trying to get Wile E. Coyote to run into the wall," a reference to the Looney Tunes cartoon.

"A f--king farce. Fake bulls--t," someone wrote. "Sums up Trump's entire phony, miserable f--king life."

Trump was reportedly humiliated by several mishaps at the Great American State Fair. The event kicked off with a Ferris wheel, rodeo horses, and a replica of Trump's proposed arch, an event billed for all Americans.

Staples were visible in several videos

However, a month before the festivities, nearly all of the performers backed out, claiming they had believed the fair would be bipartisan.

"In my mind, I thought this was a great way to celebrate the states and also bring people together in the way that only music can. I saw it as just a bigger version of so many state fairs I have performed at over the years, celebrating community and what makes each state special," said Grammy-nominated singer Martina McBride in a statement. "Yesterday things started changing, and what we were told is, in fact, not what is happening."

In a Truth Social post, Trump called the performers who backed out of the event "Third Rate," adding that he would give a speech that would rally the "U.S. "forward like I have done ever since being President!"

Trump also floated the idea of canceling the event in favor of a rally. "We should have a giant MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN RALLY, for 250, instead of having overpriced singers, who nobody wants to hear, whose music is boring, and yet who do nothing but complain," Trump wrote.

It comes after a chilling discovery was made at the bottom of the Washington DC Reflecting Pool that exposes Trump.
